results.title: The $6.88 hour: what a GPU actually costs on EC2, and when Bedrock tokens win
highlights:
Published November 6, 2026

EC2 and Bedrock price the same NVIDIA silicon through two different accounting systems. EC2 sells you the hour whether the card produced anything or not. Bedrock sells you the tokens that came out.

An H100 hour in us-east-1 is $6.88 on-demand. That same $6.88 buys about 50,000 output tokens at the most expensive text model on Bedrock, $137.50 per million. Below some volume of generated text, renting the card is the more expensive way to buy the same work, and the line falls somewhere you can actually compute.

## The ladder from T4 to B300 runs 34x, and it is not smooth

Prices are us-east-1, Linux, on-demand, from our EC2 dataset, divided by GPU count for the per-GPU rate.

| Instance | GPU | CC | VRAM (total) | $/hr | $/GPU‑hr |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| g4dn.xlarge | NVIDIA T4 | 7.5 | 16 GB | $0.5260 | $0.5260 |
| g6.xlarge | NVIDIA L4 | 8.9 | 24 GB | $0.8048 | $0.8048 |
| g5.xlarge | NVIDIA A10G | 8.6 | 24 GB | $1.0060 | $1.0060 |
| g6e.xlarge | NVIDIA L40S | 8.9 | 48 GB | $1.8610 | $1.8610 |
| p4d.24xlarge | NVIDIA A100 | 8.0 | 320 GB (8x40) | $21.9576 | $2.7447 |
| p4de.24xlarge | NVIDIA A100 (80 GB) | 8.0 | 640 GB (8x80) | $27.4471 | $3.4309 |
| p5.4xlarge | NVIDIA H100 | 9.0 | 80 GB | $6.8800 | $6.8800 |
| p5en.48xlarge | NVIDIA H200 | 9.0 | 141 GB/GPU | $63.2960 | $7.9120 |
| p6-b200.48xlarge | NVIDIA B200 | 10.0 | 1,432 GB (8x179) | $113.9328 | $14.2416 |
| p6-b300.48xlarge | NVIDIA B300 | 10.0 | 2,144 GB (8x268) | $142.4160 | $17.8020 |

The per-GPU spread is 34x from the T4 to the B300, and it steps rather than climbs: the H100 costs 2.5x the A100, the B200 costs 2.1x the H100. Monthly equivalents get absurd quickly. One p5.4xlarge is $5,022/month. A p5.48xlarge is $40,179/month.

...

An H100 crams 80 GB into its $6.88, landing at $0.0860/GB-hr, the most expensive gigabyte of VRAM in the P-series. The B200 moves 179 GB per card and lands at $0.0796 despite a GPU-hour more than double. The B300, the most expensive hour in the dataset, is still cheaper per gigabyte than the H100.

...

| H200 (`p5en`) | 9.0 | $7.9120 | $0.8791 |

...

The figures, pricing tiers, and specifications in this article were accurate at the time of writing and reflect a snapshot in time. Cloud providers frequently adjust pricing, terms, and availability. We do not continuously update historical articles as rates change. Always verify current pricing directly with your cloud provider or their official pricing calculator before making purchasing, architectural, or budgetary commitments. results.title: An H100 hour is $6.88 on AWS on-demand and $2.69 on RunPod Community Cloud · Actual Database
results.author: Nadia Voss
highlights:
Verified answer checked 2026-11-05 

AWS prices p5.48xlarge at $55.04 an hour for eight H100 80GB GPUs and p4d.24xlarge at $21.957642 an hour for eight A100 40GB GPUs in us-east-1, which is $6.88 and $2.7447 per GPU-hour (calculated 2026-11-05). RunPod lists the H100 SXM at $2.69 an hour on Community Cloud and $3.99 on Secure Cloud, with the A100 PCIe at $1.19 and $1.79 (checked 2026-11-05). That makes the list-price gap 2.56 times on H100 and 2.31 times on A100 (calculated 2026-11-05). A 730-hour month on p5.48xlarge is $40,179.20 against $15,709.60 for eight H100 SXM hours on Community Cloud (calculated 2026-11-05).

...

On 2026-11-05 an H100 80GB hour cost $2.69 on RunPod's Community Cloud, while the same class of card inside an AWS p5.48xlarge worked out to $6.88 an hour. Neither figure is the price of a GPU. Both are prices of a machine that happens to contain eight of them, and the division between the two is where GPU budgets usually go wrong.

...

| --- | --- | --- |
| AWS p5.48xlarge, us-east-1, 8 × H100 80GB | $55.04 per hour | AWS EC2 on-demand price feed |

| AWS p4d.24xlarge, 8 × A100 40GB | $21.957642 per hour | same feed |
| RunPod H100 SXM, Community / Secure | $2.69 / $3.99 per hour | RunPod pricing |

highlights:

The price per GPU-hour is derived. It is the provider's listed instance price divided by the number of GPUs on the provider's own specification page: $55.04 per instance-hour for 8 GPUs is $6.88 per GPU-hour.

Each provider's price is its own. The tracker never averages or blends prices across providers.

Both answers are from 4 November 2026, snapshot compute-2026-W45, with the AWS Price List read on 2026-11-04. Prices move: the same call on another day can give a different answer.

results.title: AWS vs Azure vs GCP Cloud GPU Pricing [2026]
results.author: Sana Rahman
highlights:
What AWS has not done, at least not in any officially confirmed source available as of October 23, 2026, is publish a flat on-demand hourly price for P5, P5e, P5en or P6-B200. Capacity Block pricing is explicitly dynamic, and AWS’s public materials direct buyers to request a quote or check the Capacity Blocks console rather than read a rate card.

...

| H200, 8-GPU node | No flat rate published | No flat on-demand VM rate confirmed in official sources | Not published |
| B200, per GPU-hour (Capacity Block) | $14.208/hour, effective Oct. 7, 2026, up from $12.355/hour (about a 15% increase) | Not offered / not confirmed | Not published; A4 uses Flex-start scheduling instead of a flat rate |

...

The single clearest pricing move any of the three providers made in the last three months was AWS’s. Effective October 7, 2026, AWS raised its P6-B200 Capacity Block price from $12.355 to $14.208 per accelerator-hour, an increase of approximately 15%, according to GPU-pricing trackers Axis Intelligence and Dev.to’s FastGPU column, which independently captured the same before-and-after figures. For an eight-GPU P6-B200 node, the current instance-hour rate is about $113.666, a noticeable jump in monthly spend for teams running sustained training jobs.

results.title: GPU Prices 2026: H100 From $3.49/hr, RTX 5070 at +58%
results.author: Axis Intelligence Research
highlights:
AWS’s per-accelerator figure that we verified is the EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML rate — a reservation you book for a fixed window, not open-ended on-demand. On October 2, 2026 the p5.48xlarge (8x H100) Capacity Block rate in US East (N. Virginia) was $41.528 per instance-hour, or $5.191 per H100. AWS’s pricing page states that from October 7, 2026, the P5 rate becomes $5.970 per accelerator across all available regions. Axis Intelligence Research did not verify a current AWS on-demand p5 rate for this snapshot, so AWS is excluded from the on-demand table rather than estimated.

...

AWS publishes the ... The October 7, 2026 update moves every GPU family up by the same proportion.

### AWS EC2 Capacity Block rate change, effective October 7, 2026

| Instance family | GPU | Rate before (per accelerator-hour) | Rate from Oct 7, 2026 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P6-B300 | B300 | $14.040 | $16.146 | +15.0% |
| P6-B200 | B200 | $12.355 | $14.208 | +15.0% |
| P5en | H200 | $6.865 | $7.895 | +15.0% |
| P5e | H200 | $5.970 | $6.866 | +15.0% |
| P5 | H100 | $5.191 | $5.970 | +15.0% |
| P4de | A100 80GB | $2.214 | $2.546 | +15.0% |
| P4d | A100 40GB | $1.475 | $1.696 | +15.0% |

Source: AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML pricing, retrieved October 2, 2026. “Before” rates are the US East (N. Virginia) or US-region rates listed on the same page; percentage change is an Axis Intelligence Research calculation.

A uniform 15% move across seven GPU generations — including a 2020-era A100 40GB — tells you this is not a scarcity signal about one chip.

results.title: AWS is raising GPU instance prices by ~20% on July 1 — and quietly keeping its own Trainium chips at
results.author: Paul Nugent
highlights:
AWS is raising GPU instance prices by ~20% on July 1 — and quietly keeping its own Trainium chips at the same price.

This is the most important AI infrastructure pricing story of the year, and the signal is unmistakable.

The move: ~20% price increase on EC2 Capacity Block reservations for Nvidia GPU instances, effective July 1. AWS cited "supply and demand dynamics" — meaning the global compute crunch has gotten severe enough that AWS believes customers will pay more without leaving.

results.title: Cloud GPU Pricing 2026: H100, B200 and RTX Rental Costs
results.author: Boris Sedu
highlights:
- Prices rose in 2026. Nebius raised on-demand prices by about 17–21% on October 1, AWS raised Capacity Block prices three times, and several clouds moved the H100 from $2.99 to $3.99 per hour.

...

The table shows typical on-demand prices per GPU-hour in the US at the end of October 2026, with examples from specific providers. Hyperscaler prices are calculated from 8-GPU instances. The low end of each range usually comes from GPU marketplaces, where prices depend on the individual host.

| GPU | Memory | Typical price per GPU-hour | Examples (on-demand) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA RTX 4090 | 24 GB | $0.30–0.90 | Vast.ai from about $0.30; RunPod $0.89 |
| NVIDIA RTX 5090 | 32 GB | $0.50–1.20 | Vast.ai from about $0.50; RunPod $1.19 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 48 GB | $0.90–1.90 | RunPod $1.09; Nebius from $1.55; AWS g6e.xlarge $1.86 |
| NVIDIA A100 | 80 GB | $0.70–3.50 | marketplaces under $1; RunPod $1.79; Lambda $2.79; AWS p4de $3.43 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 96 GB | $2–3 | RunPod $2.49 |
| NVIDIA H100 | 80 GB | $2–12.30 | Vast.ai $2.14; Lambda $3.99; RunPod $3.99 (SXM); Nebius $4.50; AWS $6.88; Google Cloud $11.06; Azure $12.29 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 141 GB | $5–8 | RunPod $5.29; Nebius $5.40; AWS p5en about $7.91 |
| NVIDIA B200 | 180 GB | $6.70–14.30 | Lambda $6.69; RunPod $7.99; Nebius $8.50; AWS p6-b200 $14.24 |
| NVIDIA B300 | 288 GB | $9–18 | RunPod $8.99; Nebius $9.50; AWS p6-b300 $17.80 |

...

- Nebius raised on-demand prices on October 1, 2026: H100 from $3.85 to $4.50 per hour, H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- AWS raised prices of EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML, its reserved GPU capacity, by about 15% in January 2026, by about 20% in July (P5 with H100 to $5.19 per GPU-hour, P6-B200 to $12.36) and again in October.
- RunPod and Lambda list the H100 SXM at $3.99 per hour; in spring 2026 both were quoted at $2.99 or less. RunPod’s B200 rose from about $5.89 to $7.99.
